cases.name: entry actions standing for a custom action and an assign push in their definition order
cases.test: predictableExec.test.ts > predictableExec > should call mixed custom and builtin actions in the definitions order

cases.name: an initial entry action has run once the actor has started
cases.test: predictableExec.test.ts > predictableExec > should call initial custom actions when starting a service (the flag once the actor has started; the check that it is still false comes before the actor is created, where there is nothing a step could record; the custom action is a set of the context)

cases.name: the actions of a transition taken on a raised event receive the raised event
cases.test: predictableExec.test.ts > predictableExec > should call raised transition custom actions with raised event

cases.name: the assign of a transition taken on a raised event receives the raised event
cases.test: predictableExec.test.ts > predictableExec > should call raised transition builtin actions with raised event

cases.name: a custom action between two assigns sees the context the first assign left
cases.test: predictableExec.test.ts > predictableExec > should correctly provide intermediate context value to a custom action executed in between assign actions (a spawnChild of a host actor stands for the custom action, so the input of its pending request shows the context it saw)

cases.name: three initial custom actions each see the context only the assigns before them left
cases.test: predictableExec.test.ts > predictableExec > initial actions should receive context updated only by preceding assign actions (a spawnChild of a host actor stands for each custom action, with the ids first, second and third in their order, so the input of each pending request shows the context that action saw)

cases.name: an entry sendTo reaches the child its state invokes, which answers before the start returns
cases.test: predictableExec.test.ts > predictableExec > should be possible to send immediate events to initially invoked actors (the first test of this name, at line 337)

cases.name: an entry sendTo reaches a child machine invoked by the same state
cases.test: predictableExec.test.ts > predictableExec > should deliver events sent from the entry actions to a service invoked in the same state

cases.name: an entry sendTo reaches the child its state invokes, the second test of that name
cases.test: predictableExec.test.ts > predictableExec > should be possible to send immediate events to initially invoked actors (the second test of this name, at line 507, a copy of the one at line 337)

cases.name: an exit action's sendTo reaches the child the state invokes before the child stops
cases.test: predictableExec.test.ts > predictableExec > should deliver events sent from the exit actions to a service invoked in the same state (the callback that resolves on MY_EVENT is a machine that records it)

cases.name: an invoke's input is computed from the context the entry assign of its state left
cases.test: predictableExec.test.ts > predictableExec > should create invoke based on context updated by entry actions of the same state (the expect on input.updated is the pending request's input)

cases.name: an invoke's input is computed from the raised event that entered its state
cases.test: predictableExec.test.ts > predictableExec > should call invoke creator with raised event (the fromCallback child is a host actor here, whose pending request shows the input the callback would read)

excluded.test: predictableExec.test.ts > predictableExec > should resolve initial assign actions before starting a service
excluded.reason: the only assertion reads the snapshot of an actor created and never started (createActor(machine).getSnapshot().context.called). A create step now creates the root without starting it, but the oracle records a snapshot only when an actor processes an event (the first at start()), so a create step writes nothing of the context; and xstate constructs the root only on the host's start (doc: #differences-construction), so before start there is no resolved context to compare. It would need a step that reads a created root's snapshot and a root constructed by create_actor

excluded.reason: fromCallback is not ported (out of scope for the actor layer): the invoked child is fromCallback(() => {})

excluded.test: predictableExec.test.ts > predictableExec > parent should be able to read the updated state of a child when receiving an event from it (the first test of this name, at line 271)
